body.name: Face-robust Airy finite-input and diagonal evaluation handle
body.construction:
The evaluator \(\mathsf E\) has finite-input and diagonal-output modes.  Finite-input mode receives integers \(n,k\geq1\), rationals \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), and the complete verified rational-spline record for \(\varphi_k^\dagger\).  It replays that record and verifies
\[
 \alpha_n(3T_k^\dagger+4\varepsilon)\leq1,
\]
then integrates every rational spline piece and all sign cells of \((x,h,\zeta)\), enumerates the finite response counts, allocation counts, observations, and factorial tables, and evaluates every prior and posterior-risk term in \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\).  It returns rationals \(b^-\leq b^+\) such that
\[
 b^-\leq B_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}\leq b^+,
 \qquad b^+-b^-\leq\delta,
\]
together with exact ordered-field maxima of \(G_{n,k,\varepsilon}^{\dagger,\mathrm A}(r)\) on the disjoint sets
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_n&=\left\{r:\min_a r_a>0,
\ \left\|n^{1/6}(r/n-q^\dagger)\right\|_\infty\leq n^{1/72}\right\},\\
\mathcal X_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a>0\}\setminus\mathcal L_n,\\
\mathcal Z_n&=\{r:\min_a r_a=0\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
For the attaining certificate, let \(\mathcal O_n\) be the finite observation alphabet under independent assignment with allocation \(q^\dagger\), put \(G=\lceil n^{3/4}\rceil\) and \(a_j=-1+j/G\) for \(0\leq j\leq2G\), and solve the rational linear program
\[
\begin{gathered}
\text{minimize }U\quad\text{over }(z_{\omega j},U),\\
z_{\omega j}\geq0,
\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{2G}z_{\omega j}=1
\quad(\omega\in\mathcal O_n),\\
\sum_{\omega\in\mathcal O_n}\sum_{j=0}^{2G}
P_y(\omega)z_{\omega j}\{a_j-\tau_{c^\dagger}(y)\}^2\leq U
\quad\text{for every }y\in\{0,1\}^{n\times3}.
\end{gathered}
\]
The returned feasible optimizer is a total randomized estimator and \(U\) is its exact rational worst-case risk.

In diagonal-output mode, on input \(n\), the same Turing machine generates the verified records for \(1\leq j\leq n\), refines the Airy eigenvalue interval to width at most \(2^{-n}\), puts \(\varepsilon_j=2^{-j}\), and selects an index satisfying
\(\alpha_n(3T_j^\dagger+4\varepsilon_j)\leq1\), with an inadmissibility flag if none exists.  It calls finite-input mode and reports rational outward errors \(e_{\mathrm{loc},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{shell},n}\), \(e_{\mathrm{zero},n}\), and \(e_{\mathrm{pr},n}\) for the three exact maxima relative to the current Airy lower endpoint and for the primal risk relative to the current Airy upper endpoint.  Both finite-input mode and every per-sample diagonal call are total.  A cross-sample certificate additionally consists of a code for a rational-valued nonincreasing computable function \(E\), finite proofs that all four errors are at most \(E(N)\) for every \(n\geq N\), and a proof that \(E(N)\to0\).  Existence and correctness of that cross-sample extension are conclusions of \(\mathrm{thm:unequal\text{-}three\text{-}arm\text{-}allocation\text{-}tube}\), not evaluator inputs.
